ripple.company_scope: Ripple says RNTB is approved for segregated RLUSD reserve management, collateral-trustee functions and fiduciary digital-asset custody. RLUSD issuance continues through Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple’s NYDFS-regulated limited-purpose trust company; RNTB does not itself issue RLUSD.

circle.entity: First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. (operating as Circle National Trust)
circle.scope: Fiduciary digital-asset custody for Circle and affiliates at opening; USDC reserve management is a future capability. OCC decision says the national trust bank itself will not issue USDC; issuance is to remain with Circle’s NY limited-purpose trust company.

coinbase.scope: National trust charter is distinct from Coinbase exchange and does not establish proprietary XRP holdings or collateral use.

occ_charter_correction.correction: Run115/Run116 wording that Ripple/Circle final approval was company-reported pending regulator-index confirmation is superseded. OCC CAS now explicitly records Consummated/Effective dates for Ripple, Circle and Coinbase.
occ_charter_correction.limits: A national trust charter is not a retail deposit-taking or lending bank charter. Charter effectiveness does not prove operating launch, XRP balances, collateral utilization or settlement throughput.

institutional_network.interpretation: Ripple, Circle and Coinbase now each have OCC-effective national trust-bank entities, but their roles differ. Ripple’s bank is a reserve collateral trustee/custodian; Circle’s bank begins with affiliate custody while reserve management is future; Coinbase’s bank is a separate custody entity. None of these facts proves XRP proprietary buying or XRP collateral utilization.
